summary: Built an Ansible-driven VRRP failover gateway for node3 to reach node4 across the two VyOS routers (node1/node2), using node5 as the Ansible control node. node3 and node4 sit on separate private segments (10.10.10.0/24 and 10.10.20.0/24) that only node1/node2 bridge; each router now runs two VRRP groups (NET-A-GW vrid 10 on eth1, NET-B-GW vrid 20 on eth2) with node1 priority 200 (preferred master) and node2 priority 100 (backup, preempt enabled). node3's single gateway for reaching node4 is the VRRP VIP 10.10.10.254 (route 10.10.20.0/24 via that VIP); node4 symmetrically routes back via 10.10.20.254, so both directions survive either router going down. Verified with a live failover test (stopped keepalived on node1, confirmed node2 became MASTER on both groups with zero ping loss to node4, then restored node1 and confirmed it preempted back to MASTER). Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: rebooted node3, node4, node5, node1, and node2 one at a time (native `reboot`, backgrounded so the ack returned first), confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and confirmed post-restart recovery (Alpine static IP/route persisted via /etc/network/interfaces; VyOS VRRP/config persisted via `save`, node1 re-preempted to MASTER, node2 returned to BACKUP, node5's Ansible project and cluster SSH key intact) before moving to the next node, preserving VRRP quorum throughout.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1/node2 are VyOS routers each with eth0 (mgmt), eth1, eth2; node3/node4 are Alpine hosts each with eth0 (mgmt) and an unconfigured eth1
Empirically confirmed via temporary test IPs that node1/node2 eth1 bridge to node3's segment and eth1/eth2 vs eth2 bridge to node4's segment

Set up cluster SSH: installed CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY on node5, added CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY to VyOS 'vyos' user config (system login user vyos authentication public-keys) on node1/node2, and to root's authorized_keys on node3/node4 after unlocking the locked root account (shadow '!*' -> '*') to satisfy PAM
Wrote an Ansible project on node5 (/root/ansible-vrrp): inventory.ini, group_vars/all.yml, host_vars for node1-4, and playbook.yml
Playbook play 1 (routers): sets eth1/eth2 addresses and two VRRP groups (NET-A-GW vrid10, NET-B-GW vrid20) via VyOS configure/commit/save, node1 priority 200, node2 priority 100

Playbook play 2 (endpoints): bootstraps python3 via raw+apk, adds static address + post-up static route to /etc/network/interfaces via blockinfile, brings interface up, and applies the route immediately
Ran the playbook successfully against all 4 target nodes and verified idempotent-safe execution
Verified show vrrp: node1 MASTER (200) on both groups, node2 BACKUP (100)
Verified node3<->node4 reachability over the VRRP-fronted routes in both directions

Performed a live failover test: stopped keepalived on node1, confirmed node2 promoted to MASTER on both VRRP groups with a continuous ping (120/120 replies, zero loss) from node3 to node4, restarted keepalived on node1, confirmed it preempted back to MASTER and node2 returned to BACKUP
Captured healthy baselines (boot_id, VRRP state, addresses, routes, ping) on all 5 nodes

Restarted node3, node4, node5, node1, node2 one at a time via backgrounded native reboot, polled each until exec was available again, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and confirmed full recovery (persisted network config, VRRP master/backup roles, end-to-end connectivity) before proceeding to the next node

evidence.requirement: node3 has a single, persistent gateway address to reach node4 (VRRP VIP)
evidence.summary: Ansible playbook applied VRRP config to node1/node2 and static route/address to node3/node4; node3 route table shows 10.10.20.0/24 via 10.10.10.254 (VIP) and ping to node4 succeeds
show vrrp confirms node1 MASTER priority 200 on both VRRP groups, node2 BACKUP priority 100

evidence.requirement: Gateway stays available when either router is down (failover demonstrated)
evidence.summary: Stopped keepalived on node1; node2 promoted to MASTER on both groups within seconds; continuous ping from node3 to node4 logged 120/120 successful replies with zero loss during the outage

evidence.requirement: Preemption back to node1 once healthy
evidence.summary: Restarted keepalived on node1; show vrrp confirms node1 reclaimed MASTER on both groups, node2 returned to BACKUP, and node3->node4 ping still succeeds
playbook.yml on node5 (control node) configures VyOS routers (VRRP groups) and Alpine endpoints (static address + route) via ansible-playbook run against inventory.ini
